title: Asset question
author: Timely_Spirit_9053
selftext: A lot of people have a issue with AI art asset, but forgive coding, but if the goal js to make a game thats free, how is one supposed to hire an artist that expects to be paid, but you arent as wealthy as those who expect no AI assets think you are? how can this be solved?

comments.author: SixStringDream
comments.body: Its odd that of all the roles in game design, its only artists who cant do free work. You're gonna code it for free? Why? People usually expect to get paid for that activity. Find an artist who will do free work for the same reason you are writing free code.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: Id have better odds of reaching the end of a rainbow and having the leprechaun hand me his pot of gold than finding an artist willing to work for free

replies.author: SixStringDream
replies.body:
but you're a programmer working for free. know any artists who might do you a favor of a couple sketches? my wife has a friend and they are still connected from art school like 20 years ago. i just straight up asked. said I'm doing this, you're sketching all the time anyway - why not sketch out some characters within a theme and let me model them?

but even before that, I did my own sketches even though I am no artist. A LOT can be done with Opus, Blender MCP, and a raw sketch. A lot. If you never built a game before then you have just as much going against you programmatically as you do artistically and you can use AI to cross both hurdles.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body:
i doodle and design my own characters and creatures as well as in this specific case, card art and frames, relics.

What AI does is help render it better, then i use photoshop to apply manual touches, AI can fuck up in some parts, but fixing mistakes is far easier for me than rendering.

as for artists who might do me a favor for a few sketches, no and id need far more than few sketches unfortunately

https://reddit.com/link/1y11phs/video/2ia4okqgor2i1/player

replies.author: SixStringDream
replies.body: I mean you are on the path. Looks like you've come pretty far Im just saying that overall Id bank that the code itself is at about this level of maturity too, no? So what's in the way? Just keep going. Refine that artistic workflow further and further.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: nothing stands in my way, im having fun, i havent been engaging with something like this for a long time, i only wanted to find out how people consider dealing with those that complain about AI asset as if the solution is simple every time when certain limitations can exist.

replies.author: SixStringDream
replies.body: I dont think the solution is simple at all. Its complicated. Low effort work shouldn't be rewarded. But if you sketch something and have AI help you model it, you've stolen nothing. Youve done the work. The people who would gripe just because you disclosed AI usage when the game is otherwise impressive are bitter trolls who dont get what is happening. At the same time there is a lot of derivative slop going around that is earning the bad reputation.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body:
thats true, not denying slop exists, i just find developing years of skill magically even after uears of trying unfeasable

the only ones who deny the existence of talent are the talented

comments.author: Carter5on
comments.body: Don't seek approval from others. You will never satisfy everyone and you shouldn't put yourself in that situation. Do what you want and whatever it takes to make your game.

comments.author: Equal_Passenger9791
comments.body: You stop giving a shit about the people who wish you're dead and just generate the assets you need with AI, easy

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: Thats what ive been doing, and its not like i dont put effort, i generally doodle the idea and how i want it to look and photoshop mistakes away, but the post was mostly how do some people expect devs to pay artists if a game has multiple assets, i alone am close to 100 assets, and most artists expect 100 usd per asset, where am i gonna make that money if im making a free game

replies.author: Equal_Passenger9791
replies.body:
Logic was never the strong point of the anti-ai crowd. If it were they'd celebrate the greatest democratization of skill and ability to ever happen in the history of mankind.

As it is they are instead the voluntary communist death squads working to demand  predatory IP policies.

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
I'm not sure the main complaint is in relation to free games, for a free game your relationship with the customer is not the same as with paid games.  
Irrespective of what model you're pursing, the majority don't care, if it looks good/pleasing most don't care whether it was AI or human artists.  
The main problem we see all the time is bad AI art, and the zealots on the anti-side, whether they're scared of losing their jobs, against AI morally, or want to support human artists, there are a lot of opinions on the subject and you really shouldn't concern yourself with them IMO, just do the best you can and accept that there will be hate regardless what you do (Even without AI). 

P.S. there are free assets if you really want to avoid AI assets creation, but they tend to come with their own set of problems.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: Free assets found online doesnt work if you are designing characters and creatures yourself, im a writer, i dont use AI for that and i dont use AI for designing characters and creatures, but as an artist i suck, i can guarantee i would never in a million years find exact free assets untouched by AI for what i need, and thats just reality for some people.

replies.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
replies.body: Of course you wont, that's one part of the many issues that comes with free assets, they wont be tailored to your vision, and most likely you'd need to get them from different sources which would create the mismatched artstyle/identity on top, you could theoratically adjust them but odds are it will take you less time and effort to learn how to do it and create them from scratch (assuming you have the artistic talents to do so to begin with, which most of us don't). I'm not saying you should use free assets, I'm saying that's an option for people who don't want to use AI assets.

comments.author: K_kkomi
comments.body:
I think this is a difficult issue, especially for solo developers and small teams working with little or no budget.

I'm also developing games independently, and hiring artists for every asset simply isn't realistic when there's no guarantee the game will make any money.

At the same time, I understand why artists are concerned about AI-generated assets. I don't think there's one solution that works for everyone. Maybe a reasonable approach is to use AI for prototyping or placeholder assets, combine it with free or properly licensed resources, and hire artists for key assets when the budget allows.

I think the important thing is being transparent about how assets were made and respecting the licenses and rights involved. Not every small indie project has the resources of a funded studio.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body:
The problem is the expectation that every small indie dev or studio has the resources of a funded studio, because AAA studios can make impressive assets, all of a sudden you are expected to have the same funds to do it.

Then we have indie teams, which are generally tight knit friends with the promise of hopes and dreams and making a profit.

Then there is me, a dingus with a paper thin wallet but hopes and dreams of giving people a free game to enjoy, by replacing money with time to make it look the best it can be within my knowledge and ability

replies.author: K_kkomi
replies.body:
I think that's something people often overlook. Not every indie developer has a team, funding, or the ability to pay for custom assets. Some people are just trying to make something meaningful with the time and resources they have.

Honestly, I respect the fact that you're putting so much time and effort into making a free game for others to enjoy. I think that's what indie development should also be about: having an idea and finding a way to bring it to life, regardless of your budget.

Keep going! I hope your game finds the players who will appreciate all that effort.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body:
ill try as hard as i can to make it look the least slop as it can
